subject: Token split for multi-model routing and shared-context crediting
messages:
From: Liz Bennett <liz.bennett@fastpay.ai>

Cc: procurement@fastpay.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on billing for multi-model routing + shared context

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looks promising. Procurement and I are trying to map expected costs for a couple of FastPay flows before we finalize the SOW. Two quick clarifying questions on billing mechanics: 

1) Multi-model routing: some requests will route to a small retrieval model (embed+search) then to a larger generator model. Do you meter tokens separately per model invocation (i.e., RAG query tokens + generator tokens billed independently), or is there a combined-metering option for pipelined calls? If separate, we need sample calculations to illustrate our expected per-transaction cost.

2) Shared-context crediting: our UX stitches a user’s recent activity (up to 6k tokens) and sends it as context to both the retrieval and generator steps. If the same context is sent to multiple models in the same logical transaction, does Redwood provide any shared-context crediting or amortization (so we aren't billed full-length context twice)? If not, is there a recommended pattern to reduce cost without hurting latency?

I attached our MAU forecast to help size things up. Procurement wants to capture this in the draft MSA pricing appendix.

Can you loop in engineering if there are any implementation caveats?

-Liz

Attachment: fastpay_mau_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Question on billing for multi-model routing + shared context

Hi Liz — great questions, thanks for sending the forecast. Short answers up top, then details below so you can paste into the pricing appendix.

TL;DR
- We bill per model invocation, counting input + output tokens for each model in the pipeline.
- We do offer amortized/shared-context credits in two cases: (a) when the same exact context bytes are used as a cached prefix within the same transaction and VM-level KV caching is enabled; (b) under an opt-in pilot for large committed customers we call "context amortization" (requires commit/enablement).

Details and examples:
1) Multi-model routing billing: each inference endpoint is metered separately by default. Example: retrieval call (400 tokens in + 8 tokens out for vectorized prompt) + generator call (500 tokens in + 200 tokens out) => billed as 408 tokens (retrieval) + 700 tokens (generator) = 1108 tokens.

2) Shared-context crediting mechanic: if you send the same 6k-token prefix to two models as independent requests, by default both invocations are billed. However: 
  - If you enable Redwood's runtime prefix caching and the second call uses the same runtime cache key within our 2-minute cache window, we can avoid charging input tokens for the cached prefix on the second invocation (you only pay for delta tokens + output).
  - Context amortization pilot: for customers with committed monthly capacity (>= $X/month) we can apply an amortization factor across pipeline stages (example: 0.6x input token charge for duplicate prefixes across the same transaction). This requires enablement and is subject to contract language.

I'll have Karthik add a technical caveat about how cache keys must be derived and where that logic lives in the client vs. server. Marissa, Vanessa — can you confirm programmatic enablement steps and what we typically require in the MSA?

Next step: we can produce a sample per-transaction cost sheet using your forecast and proposed call patterns. If that looks good I can ask Finance to bake it into the draft appendix.

-Jordan

Hi team — quick technical note to make the billing behavior predictable: 

1) Cache key derivation: our runtime cache is keyed by a stable tuple (customer_id, model_variant, prefix_hash) by default. To get cross-model prefix crediting you need to normalize the prefix hash across models (i.e., same canonical bytes). That implies the retrieval step must surface the canonicalized context (e.g., post-processing deterministic tokenization + normalization) and the generator call must use the same prefix tokenization. If you use different tokenizers or do inline enrichment between calls, you may break cache hits.

2) Latency vs. cost tradeoff: the fastest integration is a direct pipeline (call retrieval -> immediately call generator with prefix included). To save cost you can instead: 
  a) Stream the prefix into the generator only once and have the retrieval model write lightweight metadata (ids, not full text). This reduces duplicated input tokens but increases implementation complexity.
  b) Use our KV prefix cache to store the 6k prefix server-side and reference a short cache key on subsequent model invocations (that reduces network payloads too).

3) Auditing/visibility: when cache credits are applied we add a token-level adjustment line item on the invoice ("prefix cache credit") with trace IDs so you can reconcile on your side. For legal/procurement, we'll include the exact wording and sample invoice rows in the appendix.

Happy to help with a sample integration snippet — Jordan, suggest we hand this to Marissa for the pricing worksheet and to Vanessa for enablement steps.

-Karthik
